extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, opponents, and patent attorneys involved in European Patent Office (EPO) opposition and appeal proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guide to initiating, conducting and appealing oppositions against European patents before EPO Opposition Divisions and the Boards of Appeal, including grounds, timing, amendment/admission rules, representation, and strategic/national-coordination considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings may be initiated against a European patent within nine months after publication of the mention of its grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File within nine months of grant mention; no legal interest needs to be proven; oppositions filed late are inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition may be filed by any natural or legal person; a 'straw man' (person with no real interest acting for another) is admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement to prove legal interest; used both reactively (to infringement actions) and precautionarily against competitor patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for revocation (admissible grounds of opposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent may only be opposed on the grounds that: (1) the subject-matter of one or more claims is not patentable (in particular not novel or not inventive); (2) the patent does not disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art; (3) the subject-matter of the patent extends beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other grounds (e.g., lack of clarity of claims or 'theft' of the invention) are not admissible as opposition grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination limited to opposed subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division is bound to the extent to which the patent has been opposed; it will not examine subject-matter (e.g., independent claims) that have not been attacked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents should ensure they attack all claims they want examined; proprietor defenses on unopposed claims may not be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to submit known evidence and prior art before opposition period expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents should cite all known evidence and, in particular, all known prior art against the patent under opposition before the expiry of the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the opposition period, admission of new facts/evidence is at the Opposition Division’s discretion; discretion exercised restrictively especially after time limits set in the summons to oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Division composition and use of legal/technical members
rubrics_metrics.description: An Opposition Division generally consists of three technically qualified members and may be enlarged by a legal member if complex legal questions arise; a legal member is generally called for taking evidence on alleged prior public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of Division follows the technical field; panels bring several years of examination experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-instance written exchange and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of the opposition period, the EPO sets a four-month deadline for the proprietor to respond to the opposition(s); parties may be invited to submit further replies within specified time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This written exchange forms the core case file before oral proceedings; parties should prepare full submissions within these deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings and preliminary opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested (which is the rule), the Opposition Division summons the parties to oral proceedings and includes a non-binding preliminary opinion indicating issues considered relevant and possible preliminary assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary opinion helps parties focus on issues for oral proceedings; oral proceedings typically take one or two days (may be by video conference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be occasioned by a ground of opposition and not extend protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments may be chosen from the whole content of the original patent application’s disclosure as long as the scope of protection is not extended beyond the granted patent’s scope; amendments need to be occasioned by a ground of opposition (not mere cosmetic or clarity edits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition proceedings must not be used to reformulate claims/descriptions for mere clarity or to adapt to competitors; amended claims must be directly and unambiguously derivable from the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary requests ranking and admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may defend the patent by a main request and one or more auxiliary requests; an auxiliary request is considered only if the main request or a higher-ranking auxiliary request is found not to meet EPC requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of new requests is procedurally limited; requests submitted in oral proceedings are usually not admitted unless they can be readily discussed by the panel and opponent or are reactions to new objections made in oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on late/new requests and late submissions at oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests submitted in oral proceedings are, as a rule, not admitted unless readily discussable or reacting to a new objection; primarily only small editorial amendments are permitted during oral proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should present prepared claim sets and defenses in earlier rounds; reliance on the oral proceedings to introduce major new claim sets is risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal time limits and statement of grounds requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party adversely affected by an Opposition Division decision may appeal within two months after receipt of the written decision; the appellant has an additional two months to submit reasoning. The statement of grounds of appeal shall contain the appellant’s complete case, including all legal and technical arguments and any modified main and auxiliary requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits are not extendible; appeals may be rejected as inadmissible if they do not deal with the appealed decision or fail to present a complete case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of Appeal discretion on admissibility of new facts/evidence/requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards of Appeal admit new facts, evidence or requests considering relevance, complexity, the current state of proceedings and the need for procedural economy; submissions that could have been made earlier or were rejected in first instance may be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions requiring cancellation/postponement of oral proceedings are generally not admitted; Boards increasingly act as reviewing bodies and reject arguments that put the case on a new footing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and interpretation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party may use any of the three official EPO languages (English, German, French). Oral proceedings are held in the language of the proceedings (the language in which the application was published). Communications and final decisions are issued in the language of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation between the three official languages is provided on prior request at no extra cost; parties may nonetheless express themselves in any official language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and expert testimony practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition Divisions and Boards decide based on their own technical expertise; appointment of a technical expert ex officio is rare. Parties may present private experts who can submit written opinions and, with prior notice, attend oral proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private experts are the usual route for technical evidence; relying on ex officio experts is uncommon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may be represented by a professional representative admitted to practice before the EPO, in particular by a European Patent Attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European Patent Attorneys commonly handle opposition proceedings; coordination with national attorneys may be needed when parallel national litigation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of opponent withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Although an opponent may withdraw the opposition at any time, withdrawal does not necessarily terminate the opposition proceedings; the Opposition Division may continue proceedings on its own motion and issue a decision within the framework of the original opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal of the (only) appeal will, however, terminate the second-instance appeal proceedings. Consider this when negotiating settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention by defendant in infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant in national patent infringement proceedings may intervene in pending opposition proceedings within three months from the institution of infringement proceedings; the defendant must accept the opposition proceedings at their current stage but may introduce new grounds and submit new facts/evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no opposition is pending, defendants must decide strategically whether to file an opposition within nine months or start national invalidity proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic interplay with national invalidity/infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: National courts (e.g., German Federal Patent Court) may apply different substantive standards (e.g., a somewhat higher inventive step hurdle) and national invalidity actions may be barred while an opposition is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing strategy must weigh risks that a third party might file an opposition and block national nullity suits; coordination and early communication with potentially affected competitors is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to accelerate proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties involved in patent infringement proceedings may request acceleration of the opposition proceedings and subsequent appeal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceleration requests are possible but subject to the EPO’s discretion and case circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation and exceptional apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party generally bears its own costs, including official fees for filing an opposition or an appeal. An apportionment of costs may exceptionally be ordered where an abuse of procedure has taken place and the adversary had to bear superfluous costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of abuse: failing to inform the EPO in due time that a party will not be represented at appointed oral proceedings, leading the other party to incur unnecessary costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of opposition decisions across designated states
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision in opposition proceedings is retroactively effective in all states where the opposed patent is valid. If maintained in amended form, the patent must be revalidated in all designated states, generally requiring translations and additional costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National invalidity proceedings after the opposition period (or terminated opposition) may produce differing results country-by-country; be aware of downstream national requirements and costs for revalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural law and governing instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings are governed by the European Patent Convention (EPC), the Implementing Regulations and the Guidelines (Part D); appeal proceedings follow the Rules of Procedure of the Boards of Appeal. The Boards of Appeal are not bound to apply the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with EPC, Implementing Regulations, Guidelines (Part D) and Rules of Procedure is necessary; Boards may exercise independent procedural judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of new grounds of opposition after the opposition period
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of new grounds of opposition after the expiry of the opposition period is subject to procedural restrictions; in first-instance proceedings a new ground may be examined if the Opposition Division considers it prima facie relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on early, comprehensive pleadings; late new grounds face higher hurdles and limited discretion for admission.
